title: Tenant-aware Tempo ingest adapter with ordered ACKs and dead-letter handling
creator: Priya Natarajan
description: Build a Tempo-compatible ingest adapter that sits in front of our Tempo/OTLP export path to handle legacy batched span envelopes (Zipkin/Jaeger HTTP batches, older OTLP variants). The adapter must: (1) accept multiple legacy formats and normalize to OTLP v1; (2) perform per-tenant rate adaptation and backpressure to prevent noisy tenants from impacting others; (3) provide ordered ACK semantics for fanout scenarios so that downstream replays/dual-writes maintain causal ordering where required; (4) surface malformed or unverifiable batches to a dead-letter store with metadata for debugging; and (5) expose tracing and SLO metrics for ingestion latency, queue depth, dropped/bounced batches, and dead-letter rates. This component will be deployed as a regional, horizontally-scalable service alongside the existing OTLP ingress gateway and will be the primary compatibility shim during a phased migration of legacy clients.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Adapter accepts Zipkin/Jaeger/OTLP HTTP batches and emits OTLP gRPC to Tempo with schema-normalized Resource/Span attributes; 2) Per-tenant throughput limits enforced (configurable) and respected under load; 3) Ordered ACK mode preserves sequence for fanout ops (can replay in order) and provides idempotency keys to Tempo where supported; 4) Non-conforming batches are routed to dead-letter storage with an index entry and retain original payload for 7 days; 5) Dashboard exists showing ingestion latency percentiles, per-tenant rate limits hit, live DLQ count, and overall success ratio; 6) Canary rollout shows zero error-rate regression for golden traces and <=3% increase in p99 ingest latency during peak test compared to baseline.
implementation_notes:
- Protocol: accept HTTP/JSON (Zipkin), HTTP Thrift/JSON (Jaeger), legacy OTLP/HTTP and OTLP/gRPC. Normalize to OTLP proto v1.
- Transport: use persistent gRPC stream to Tempo with windowed ACKs (application-level) to enable ordered ack semantics without blocking throughput.
- Backpressure: token-bucket per-tenant + global circuit-breaker; use in-memory fast-path for hot tenants and Redis for slower counters to survive restarts.
- Ordering: attach monotonic sequence numbers per-tenant; record last-acked seq in lightweight metadata store (Dynamo/etcd) for resume.
- Dead-letter: store raw batch to S3 (or regional object store) and write index (tenant, seq, reason, pointer) to Postgres for quick lookup.
- Idempotency: add deterministic digest header and propagate to Tempo when supported; otherwise rely on sequence window and replay guard in downstream.
- Observability: emit metrics (prometheus) and distributed traces for adapter internal flow; add alerts for DLQ growth, repeated malformed patterns, and tenant throttling spikes.
- Config: tenant rate configs pulled from Console feature flags + fallback defaults.
- Performance targets: 20k spans/s sustained per instance with p50 ingest < 30ms and p99 < 250ms in regional tests.
- Correlate with existing ingest gateway code-paths (ENG-271001) to avoid double-conversion and to reuse auth/tenant extraction logic.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for format parsers (Zipkin/Jaeger/OTLP) with edge cases (missing timestamps, null traceid, negative duration).
- Integration: local Tempo instance + test harness that can emit mixed-format batches; validate normalization and ordering with synthetic sequences.
- Load tests: run k6/geth-style generator to reach 20k spans/s per instance across tenants (uniform and skewed distributions) to validate per-tenant throttling and backpressure behavior.
- Fault-injection: simulate Tempo gRPC failures, delayed acks, and object-store write errors to ensure DLQ and retry semantics behave as designed.
- Security: fuzz inputs to ensure there are no header/attribute injection vectors; include scanning in CI.
- E2E: canary in staging with selected production tenants for 48h, monitor dashboards and rollback on DLQ spike or >5% error-rate increase.
rollout_plan:
1) Deploy adapter in 'compat' mode but route only a small percentage (1%) of legacy traffic through it for verification. 2) Monitor metrics for 24h, validate no delta on golden trace set. 3) Increase to 10% for 24h, validate, then 50% for 24h. 4) Flip clients gradually by region/tenant. 5) After 2 weeks of stable metrics, promote adapter to default ingress for legacy formats and start deprecating older gateway paths. 6) Final cleanup: remove legacy parsing code from gateway after 90 days of stable operation and coordinate with customers.
Fallbacks: automatic circuit-breaker will drop/redirect to existing gateway if DLQ or error rates exceed thresholds; playbook documented in links below.
